title: Shape buildings with recipe handles.
description: Recipe-authored gold handles reshape a connected temple and gallery. Move a source, retain its doorway and roof links, and save your own edition.
prompt: Create a detailed Japanese temple garden with procedural materials, repeated shared geometry and reflected stone floors. Keep building composition in declarative recipes. Add useful bounded input.handle controls for the hall roof rise and doorway width, and the gallery width, length and passage height. Expose the Constructions HUD. Inspect bindings, preview connections and estimate changes. Preserve stable IDs, overrides and existing content. Save and reopen the full scene.
control_note: Requires an existing hall and commands.recipe_handles. Selects the Constructions HUD; it does not create a building. Inspect parameter_schema for bindings before editing.

experiments.title: Give useful controls to the user
experiments.text: Open & test → Adjust → Open construction handles. Choose hall and Shape. Drag a gold roof-rise or doorway-width guide; release to validate, Escape to cancel.

experiments.title: Free the view
experiments.text: Use Hide panel, keep handles on a narrow screen. Click a labelled base dot to select another instance. Reopen Constructions to choose Move or Rotate; moving a source keeps its declared dependent gallery aligned.

experiments.title: Keep recipes editable
experiments.text: Add input.handle metadata to bounded numeric recipe inputs, preserving existing params. Other inputs keep their sliders. Save my scene stores values, declarations, materials and relationships.

viewer_note: Handles are generic local-axis value guides with numeric origins, not building-specific generators. Geometry validates and rebuilds once on release. Fixed origins do not automatically follow other dimensions. Attached roots stay constrained; detach explicitly before free movement. Pause playback before editing. Reflections remain recipe settings.

title: Connect through a real doorway.
description: Connect an independent gallery to a real exported doorway. Preview a compatible port, align its threshold and keep both recipes editable.
prompt: In Polynite, discover architecture connections and the anchor/wall operators. Use an editable assembly recipe: export entrance from the hall wall opening and declare a root entry anchor on the gallery. Inspect both IDs, preview architecture.connections for gallery/from with target hall, then estimate and apply attach:{to:hall,anchor:entrance,from:back000000}. Keep the roof context link and recipes independent. Use compatible doorway dimensions, shared procedural materials and instances. Move/rotate/resize the provider and verify that the thresholds stay aligned and the walls leave a real passage. Preserve overrides; save and reopen the complete scene. Enable soft floor reflections in scene settings.
control_note: Read-only fit preview for existing instances. Inspect their real port IDs first; estimate and apply the separate attachment patch only after checking compatibility.

experiments.title: Find a connection
experiments.text: Open & test → Adjust → gallery · connections. Find compatible connections, choose hall · entrance, then Connect and align. Incompatible ports show a reason.

experiments.title: Give the doorway a size
experiments.text: Under hall recipe controls adjust door width. Under gallery recipe controls choose passage width and height that fit. An invalid edit keeps the last valid scene.

experiments.title: Save and continue
experiments.text: Save your independent .scene and reopen it. The two recipes, connection, roof link, materials and custom parameters remain editable. Detach preserves position; explicit roof links remain until you change their recipe.

viewer_note: The engine aligns typed interfaces and validates transactions. Real passage exports come from wall openings; a point cannot cut a wall. Profiles, frames, materials, proportions and reflected floors stay in recipes. Preview checks port fit; estimate also checks roof contact, budgets and protected edits. No global welding, automatic doorway enlargement or obstacle routing.

title: Connect buildings. Keep their recipes.
description: Attach a covered gallery to a Japanese hall. Its roof, walls and access steps follow the host while both assemblies remain editable.
prompt: In Polynite discover roof, wall and context, then check commands.recipe_roof_ports. Let a provider roof export a named port, inspect roof_ports and attach an independent gallery at its authored doorway. Bind context:{name:hostroof,instance:hall,roof:main} and use roof join:@hostroof. Keep the host passage opening, gallery profiles, materials and repeated details in editable recipes. Estimate; change source proportions and pose; verify the dependent roof and walls. Preserve stable IDs and overrides, enable soft floor reflections, save and reopen the complete document.
control_note: Edit the existing hall in this example. In another scene, inspect construction IDs, anchors, roof_ports and parameter schemas before binding a consumer. Keep both recipes and their explicit dependency.

experiments.title: Lift the hall
experiments.text: Open & test → Adjust → hall · recipe controls: try rise 1.8. The attached gallery follows the doorway; its walls meet the shared roof envelope and its solid stairs reach the ground.

experiments.title: Grow the main building
experiments.text: Change hall size to 1.1. Its exported roof is sampled in the gallery frame, keeping their meeting point aligned.

experiments.title: Give the gallery more room
experiments.text: Under Adjust → gallery · recipe controls, try length 7 and width 2.7. The gallery keeps its own recipe and joins the declared host roof.

experiments.title: Save your variation
experiments.text: Save, reopen and continue editing the existing hall and gallery. Materials, parameters, attachment and roof context are retained.

experiments.title: Compare the reflected floor
experiments.text: Floor reflections are enabled in this scene. Keep them while comparing proportions, or adjust the floor reflection strength to suit your own material.

viewer_note: The engine supplies generic roof ports, envelope clipping, wall openings, assembly transforms and shared geometry. Roof profiles, timber details, layout and floor appearance belong to recipes. This is a directed provider-to-consumer join: the provider keeps its authored roof; separate wall chains are not globally welded. Consumers must overlap and contact the declared source roof. Use Open & test → Adjust to change the controls.

title: Join a roof. Open a doorway.
description: Compose a Japanese hall with roofs that meet, real openings and shared timber details. Change its proportions, then save and reopen your variation.
prompt: In Polynite, discover architecture.operators for roof and wall and check commands.recipe_junctions. Compose an editable Japanese temple from a local joined roof and mitered wall chain. Cut the door and windows as real openings. Keep curvature, door width, materials and ornament choices in a module:assembly recipe; use shared prototypes for columns and repeated brackets. Estimate before applying. Change the roof rise and door width, inspect contacts and voids, save, reopen and resume by patching the same instance ID. Preserve the current scene.
control_note: This changes the hall in this example. In another scene, discover the existing construction ID and its parameter schema first. Keep the same instance when continuing; do not replace the scene.

experiments.title: Make room at the entrance
experiments.text: In Scene settings → Living architecture → hall, set door_width to 1.65. The opening and its timber frame widen together.

experiments.title: Change the silhouette
experiments.text: Try rise 1.8 and eave_lift 0.2. Wall tops continue to meet the roof underside.

experiments.title: A smaller courtyard building
experiments.text: Set size to 0.85. The joined shell, columns, details and access steps scale as one assembly.

experiments.title: Keep your own version
experiments.text: Save the scene, reopen it and continue editing hall. Its recipe, procedural materials and current values travel together.

viewer_note: The engine supplies reusable roof, wall, surface and assembly operators. The Japanese profiles, materials and ornament choices belong to the editable recipe. Find all six controls under Scene settings → Living architecture → hall; the Showcase viewer also has Adjust. Rectangular openings and local roof joins are supported; separate wall chains are not globally welded.

title: A colourful tower
description: Start with 28 blocks, then make it your own.
prompt:
Create a colourful procedural tower in Polynite.

- Build seven layers of four cubes, alternating cyan, pink and yellow.
- Frame the whole tower and make a smooth five-second camera orbit.
- Add a short animated 3D title reading BUILD SOMETHING.

title: A burst of colour
description: Launch, freeze the action, orbit and let it tumble.
prompt:
Create a colourful physics block explosion in Polynite.

- Arrange 64 cubes as a compact cluster and launch them outwards with collisions and gravity.
- Show an animated EXPLODE title, a brief camera push and subtle impact sound.
- Freeze the action briefly, orbit around the suspended debris, then resume the fall.
- Keep the whole effect visible in a replayable Cinematic sequence.

title: Brick wall lab
description: Tune the impact, dust and render budget with 17 scene-owned controls.
prompt:
Create an advanced procedural brick-wall demolition scene in Polynite.

- Generate a staggered wall of 30 rows by 10 columns of individually simulated red clay bricks, with rough grain, small bevels and seeded colour variation.
- Suspend a dark steel wrecking ball from 18 alternating physical chain links and swing it through the wall. Use a textured aggregate floor, contact shadows and warm/cool lighting.
- Define scene-owned MCP custom values: impact speed 6 m/s (1–15), ball mass 100 kg (10–100), brick mass 2 kg (0.5–10), friction 0.85 (0.1–1.5), release angle 33° (5–55), rows 30 (5–30), and chain visibility.
- Add dust controls: enabled, amount 0.85 (0–1), size 0.28 m (0.02–0.75), lifetime 2.4 s (0.2–4), opacity 0.65 (0–1), and minimum impact energy 1 J (0–100).
- Add render quality Mobile/Balanced/Export, motion blur 0 (0–1), brick bevel 0.004 m (0–0.008), and colour variation 0.075 (0–0.3).
- Define English-labelled Gentle, Breach, Demolition, Mobile and Cinematic presets. Mobile uses 18 rows, lighter LOD and dust, and no motion blur.
- Author a roughly ten-second replayable Cinematic sequence: start with the intact wall, release the ball, then orbit gently through the collision and falling debris.
control_note: These MCP arguments select an existing preset. The creation prompt above asks the assistant to define all custom values and their bindings when building the scene.

items.label: Impact speed
items.hint: Initial push in metres per second. Increase speed before reducing brick mass.

items.label: Ball mass
items.hint: A heavier ball carries more momentum at the same speed.

items.label: Brick mass
items.hint: Heavier bricks resist the impact; lighter bricks scatter more easily.

items.label: Brick friction
items.hint: Higher friction reduces sliding after the impact.

items.label: Release angle
items.hint: Starting angle of the suspended ball, measured in degrees.

items.label: Wall rows
items.hint: Generate a shorter or taller wall without placing each brick manually.

items.label: Show chain
items.hint: Show or hide the link meshes; the suspension physics remains active.

items.label: Impact dust
items.hint: Enable the bounded collision-particle effect.

items.label: Dust amount
items.hint: More visible dust without creating more physical bodies.

items.label: Cloud size
items.hint: Size of the individual dust puffs, in metres.

items.label: Cloud lifetime
items.hint: How long each puff remains visible.

items.label: Dust opacity
items.hint: Control transparency separately from cloud size and lifetime.

items.label: Minimum impact energy
items.hint: Only collisions above this energy emit dust. Lower it for gentler impacts.

items.label: Render quality
items.hint: Mobile uses lighter geometry and effects; Balanced is the everyday profile; Export uses full meshes.

items.label: Motion blur
items.hint: Rigid-object motion blur. It is disabled by the Mobile profile.

items.label: Brick edge radius
items.hint: Small bevels catch light along the edges. This remains bounded for the physics shape.

items.label: Brick colour variation
items.hint: Seeded colour variation shared by the procedural wall recipe.

experiments.title: 1. Gentle versus Demolition
experiments.text: Try Gentle (50 kg ball, 6 kg bricks, 2 m/s), then Demolition (100 kg ball, 0.75 kg bricks, 12 m/s). Apply and replay each preset; compare the opening and the debris.

experiments.title: 2. Make dust easier to see
experiments.text: Use Breach, then increase cloud size to 0.4 m and lifetime to 3 s. Change only one value at a time. On an updated viewer, lower the energy threshold for lighter impacts.

experiments.title: 3. Build for a phone
experiments.text: Choose Mobile: 18 rows, no motion blur and bounded dust. Check responsiveness on a real phone. Visual LOD does not change the physical colliders.

experiments.title: 4. Frame and record
experiments.text: Choose Cinematic for a desktop video. Preview with a free camera or at 0.5x, then record the authored sequence as MP4. Save the .scene alongside the video to keep the controls.

viewer_note: Live effects/body properties and queued initial-setup edits need the latest viewer. Earlier viewers either queue all edits or reset on release, and may omit dust opacity/energy threshold. Live grabbing, camera modes and speed controls also require a recent build.

title: Words in orbit
description: A real 3D ring of letters around a simple shape.
prompt:
Create a cyan sphere with a golden 3D ring of letters in Polynite.

- Make the ring read CREATE / VIEW / SHARE, anchored in world space around the sphere.
- Rotate the letters slowly and orbit the camera for about six seconds.
- Use soft lighting and keep the whole ring readable.

title: Your first three shapes
description: Create, recolour and resize three simple objects.
prompt:
Create a cyan cube, a pink sphere and a golden cone side by side in Polynite.

- Use contrasting silhouettes on a reflective ground plane.
- Make the objects appear with a subtle blue edge reveal.
- Create a smooth six-second Cinematic camera orbit that keeps all three shapes in view.

title: Let gravity do the work
description: Watch blocks and balls fall, bounce and settle.
prompt:
Create a colourful gravity-and-collision demo in Polynite.

- Arrange eight dynamic cubes and four dynamic spheres above a solid ground plane.
- Let them fall, bounce and settle with realistic collisions and subtle impact sounds.
- Pause the initial pose briefly, then release the simulation and orbit the camera for about seven seconds.
- Keep the initial state and sequence replayable.

title: A closer look
description: Move from a close detail to a smooth wider orbit.
prompt:
Create a small colourful sculpture made from six cubes in Polynite.

- Begin with a close view of one detail.
- Pull the camera back over about 2.4 seconds to reveal the whole sculpture.
- Blend smoothly into a four-second orbit, keeping the subject inside the frame.

title: A command comes to life
description: Animated typing, quiet cues and a glowing confirmation.
prompt:
Create a cyan cube and a pink sphere in Polynite, then animate a command confirmation.

- Use command-input-v2 to type Make it blue in an illustrative command overlay, with discreet sounds and a glowing checkmark.
- After confirmation, turn the sculpture blue and fade the overlay gently.
- Create a roughly six-second camera orbit around the updated sculpture.
control_note: This snippet adds the illustrative command field only. The blue colour change is a separate action in the downloadable scene.

title: Make the ending yours
description: Keep the Polynite signature, choose its placement and soften its sound.
prompt:
Create a simple cyan cube and pink sphere scene in Polynite with a customised film ending.

- Make a smooth 4.5-second camera orbit.
- Use polynite-ending-v4 with the required Polynite signature in the short-portrait layout, placed higher in the frame, and sound volume 0.5.
- Keep the scene fade, shine-only bloom and discreet ending sounds coordinated.
- Record a portrait MP4 to show the ending; keep the live scene preview free of the closing signature.

title: From scene to MP4
description: Record a smooth film, preview it and keep your own copy.
prompt:
Create and record a small procedural sculpture in Polynite.

- Arrange nine colourful spheres above a softly reflective ground plane.
- Add a subtle appearance reveal and a smooth six-second Cinematic camera orbit.
- Record the authored sequence from its initial state as a landscape MP4 at 1080p and 60 FPS, with discreet sounds.
- Wait for completion, then provide the actual downloadable MP4 and an editable .scene containing the scene and its sequence.

title: A forest under colourful rain
description: Static tree colliders meet falling spheres and cubes.
prompt:
Create a small stylised forest under colourful rain in Polynite.

- Build tree trunks and canopies as static colliders.
- Drop ten colourful spheres and ten cubes above the forest as dynamic bodies.
- Make them collide with the trees and ground, with gravity and discreet impact sounds.
- Create a slow seven-second camera orbit that keeps the forest and collisions visible.

title: One push, a chain reaction
description: A small impulse sends a row of coloured dominos tumbling.
prompt:
Create a row of 20 colourful physics dominos in Polynite.

- Use upright blocks at least 0.10 m thick, spaced closely enough to strike the next piece when they fall.
- Give only the first domino a gentle initial tilt and angular velocity.
- Let the chain reaction unfold with realistic collisions and subtle impact sounds.
- Keep the camera close enough to see each collision in a replayable eight-second Cinematic sequence.

title: Autumn Lantern Cottage
description: A moonlit cottage, coherent seeded variants and a seamless 15-second visual loop.
prompt:
Create a warm autumn cottage diorama in Polynite with a perfect 15-second visual loop.

- Discover the connected engine capabilities. Save the current editable film and restore it after any temporary tests.
- Generate a coherent random cottage with a recorded nonzero integer seed, detail 0.68, fantasy 0.3 and roof_curve 1.15. Preserve version 1 recipes and the chosen seed for reproduction.
- Generate the dependent path, garden and trees, in that order. Place ivy around the walls while keeping windows, shutters and the door clear. Include stone paving, pumpkins and longer grass near walls and trunks.
- Use seeded cards trees with autumn foliage, count 3, detail 0.68 and leaf_density 1. Offer rounded or hybrid trees for lower budgets without silently changing style on rerolls.
- Set a blue-violet twilight sky, subtle stars and Milky Way, a cool moon above the horizon and a sun below it. Keep window and lantern light warm, with restrained bloom and god rays.
- Synchronize shared spatial wind, grass, smoke and falling leaves to 15 seconds. Leaves settle and fade on the ground. Keep sky twinkle and cloud/aurora speeds zero for this loop.
- Make one continuous 15-second camera orbit. Windows turn on with a brief rustic flicker; keep smoke anchored to the chimney. Expose scene-owned lighting, wind, vegetation and quality controls.
- Inspect real frames, compare render endpoints at 0 and 15 seconds, and save the expanded editable scene. Keep the chosen random seed; do not claim that random generation alone guarantees a perfect loop.
viewer_note: The saved example is the reference seed 0; the prompt asks for a new nonzero seed. The silent preview loops its first 15 seconds; the full film includes a short ending. Detailed cards cost more than rounded foliage. Exact visual endpoints were verified natively; this is not a claim that every physics or audio simulation loops.

title: An endless flight
description: Turn on Polynite's infinite world through MCP: a ship flies over mountains, plains, seas and red-rock mesas that never end, and the scene saves exactly.
prompt:
Create an endless flight in Polynite.

- Check scene.capabilities for the infinite operation.
- Turn it on with scene.apply {op:'infinite', on:true, seed:7, follow:3}, hide the flat floor (floor_enable 0) and keep the sky on with a warm sun.
- Add a 20-second loop_orbit camera behind the ship (front_yaw 0) and record a short film.
control_note: These arguments turn the infinite world on in the current scene. Every other dial (biomes, water, boost, effects, sound) is a named parameter listed in describe.infinite.params.

items.label: Ship speed
items.hint: Metres per second. Zero parks the ship to inspect, save and compare.

items.label: World seed
items.hint: Another seed is another world; the same seed always gives the same land.

items.label: Lake level
items.hint: The level of the lakes and of the open sea.

experiments.title: More sea, more rock
experiments.text: Ask for {op:'infinite', oceans:0.5, rocky:0.4}: the world changes around the ship without reloading.

experiments.title: Boost
experiments.text: Ask for {op:'infinite', boost_now:true}: the central reactor lights up, the ship accelerates and the camera widens.

experiments.title: Look into the sun
experiments.text: Ask for {op:'lens', on:true}: glare, star, ghosts and dazzle when the sun is in frame.

experiments.title: Every dial
experiments.text: Ask your assistant to read describe.infinite.params: terrain, biomes, water, flight, effects and sound, each with its range.

viewer_note: Requires the Polynite engine with the infinite world (web version 0308 or later, desktop current). The land is generated on your device; only the seed, the parameters, the ship and your edits are saved.

title: Your first SDF drawing
description: Draw a vector HUD over a small studio through MCP: a ring, a gauge arc, a leader line and a label, traced stroke by stroke.
prompt:
Create a small night studio in Polynite and draw a first SDF shape over it.

- Build the studio on the standard floor: a dark cylinder pedestal, a glowing cyan sphere on it, an orange cube and a pink cone beside it; deep blue floor tiles, a light floor mirror and soft bloom.
- Call scene.shape help once to read the grammar. Shapes live on a 100-unit canvas, y up; items are drawn and traced in list order.
- Upsert a screen shape with id 'first', space 'screen', at [0.6, 0.38], size 0.42, style 'hologram': a circle (r 40) with id 'ring', an arc (r 32, a0 210, a1 -30, w 3), a line from '#ring.right' to [70, 22], a polyline to [132, 22] and the text 'HELLO SDF'.
- Make it appear with in {fx:'trace', dur:2.6} and leave with out {fx:'trace', dur:1.2}; set show:'film' and add the film step {op:'shape', at:0.4, dur:10.2, id:'first'}.
- Add a slow 11-second camera orbit, record a short film and check a frame with scene.capture.

experiments.title: Another look
experiments.text: Ask for scene.shape patch {id:'first', set:[{path:'style', value:'neon'}]}: the same drawing in neon, darkpunk, vaporwave, blueprint or amber.

experiments.title: Reverse the pen
experiments.text: Add dir:-1 to the arc: it is now traced from its other end.

experiments.title: Point at it
experiments.text: Replace the line's start with '#ring.at(0.25)': references point to any earlier item by id.

control_note: These arguments add one shape to the current scene with scene.shape upsert. Ask scene.shape help for the full grammar, then check the result with scene.capture.
viewer_note: Requires the Polynite engine with SDF shapes (the scene.shape command). Shapes are saved inside the scene and replayed by its film; nothing is uploaded.

title: Filled shapes, curves and boolean ops
description: Rounded boxes, ellipses, stars, pies, SVG paths with holes, subtracted and smoothly merged shapes, dashes, repetition and a curved arrow.
prompt:
Create a gallery of filled SDF shapes in Polynite over a small night studio.

- Reuse a studio on the standard floor (pedestal, glowing sphere, cube, cone) and read scene.shape help.
- Upsert one screen shape, style 'neon', size 0.42: a rounded box (size [36,24], r 5, angle 12, fill and stroke, color 2), a green ellipse (color [0.4,1,0.55,1]), a filled star, a pie sector (r 16, a0 90, a1 -150) and a filled heart as an SVG path with two cubic curves.
- Second row: a box with a circle cut out of it (op:'subtract'), two discs merged with op:'smooth' (k 6), a dashed circle (dash [4,3]), twelve ticks from one line with repeat {radial:12, c} and a curved arrow with a dot tail.
- Trace it in over 3.2 s, fade it out, and show it with a film step {op:'shape', at:0.4, dur:11.4, id:'fills'} under a slow camera orbit.
- Check status: cost.tiles and cost.vs_one_quad show how the shape was cut into quads that fit its ink.

experiments.title: Your own outline
experiments.text: Any SVG path works: ask for {path:'M ... C ... Z', fill:true} - a logo, a leaf, a silhouette. Several sub-paths make holes.

experiments.title: Melt them
experiments.text: Raise the smooth union's k from 6 to 15: the two discs flow into one blob.

experiments.title: Compare the cost
experiments.text: Add tiles:'one' to the shape and read status.cost: one quad does the same picture with several times more work.

control_note: These arguments add one shape to the current scene with scene.shape upsert. Ask scene.shape help for the full grammar, then check the result with scene.capture.
viewer_note: Requires the Polynite engine with SDF shapes (the scene.shape command). Shapes are saved inside the scene and replayed by its film; nothing is uploaded.

title: Animated gauges with live values
description: A gauge, a progress ring, a radar, a speed readout and bars driven by one animated value; an arc spun by time.
prompt:
Create a live HUD in Polynite whose numbers move.

- Over a small night studio on the standard floor, upsert a screen shape 'live' (style 'hologram', size 0.42) with v:[0,0,0,0].
- Animate v0 with keys: {t:1, v0:0}, {t:6.5, v0:0.92}, {t:9.5, v0:0.55}. Any number in the drawing can use it: '$v0', '$v0*0.8'.
- Add widgets: gauge {value:'$v0', label:'POWER'}, progress {value:'$v0*0.8'}, radar {sweep:120, blips}, readout {label:'SPEED', value:'{v0*1200:0}', unit:'km/h'} and bars with values like '$v0' or '0.4+sin($t*3)*0.2'.
- Spin an arc with time: a0 '90-$t*120', a1 '-30-$t*120', and print the clock with text 'T+{t:1}s'.
- Show it with {op:'shape', at:0.4, dur:11.4, id:'live'} and record. Later, set values without redrawing with scene.shape values {id:'live', v:[0.3]}.

experiments.title: Drive it yourself
experiments.text: Remove the keys and send scene.shape values {id:'live', v:[0.2]}, then [0.9]: the gauge, readout and bars follow at once.

experiments.title: Count anything
experiments.text: In any text, {expression:digits} prints a value: 'FUEL {v0*100:0}%', 'T+{t:1}s'.

experiments.title: Make it loop
experiments.text: Add loop:10 to the shape: its keys repeat every ten seconds.

control_note: These arguments change the live value v0 of the 'live' shape without resending the drawing.
viewer_note: Requires the Polynite engine with SDF shapes (the scene.shape command). Shapes are saved inside the scene and replayed by its film; nothing is uploaded.

title: A HUD anchored in the world
description: A ring of ticks lying flat around an object and a label that always faces the camera, with an arrow pointing down at it.
prompt:
Create a HUD that lives in the 3D scene in Polynite.

- Build a small night studio on the standard floor with a glowing sphere at [0, 1.15, 0] on a pedestal.
- Upsert a world shape 'halo' with space 'world', p [0, 0.34, 0], face 'up' (lying flat) and size 3.2 (metres for 100 units): a circle r 48, 36 ticks from one line with repeat {radial:36}, two arcs (one in color 2). Turn it slowly with anim {rotate:0.04, pulse:0.5}.
- Upsert a world shape 'tag' at p [0, 2.45, 0], face 'camera', size 2.8: a bracket, the centred text 'CORE ORB' and an arrow down to the sphere with a dot head. Grow it in with keys {t:0, scale:0.8, opacity:0.5} to {t:1.2, scale:1, opacity:1} and a light flicker.
- World shapes are depth-tested: the sphere hides the ring where it passes behind it. Show both with film steps and record under a camera orbit.
- Anchors can follow scene objects too: to:'@model', or a point inside a drawing such as an arrow's 'to'.

experiments.title: Stand it up
experiments.text: Change the halo's face to 'camera_y': it turns to the camera but stays upright, like a sign.

experiments.title: Tilt it
experiments.text: Use face:'fixed' with pitch and roll in degrees to set the ring at any angle.

experiments.title: Read the report
experiments.text: scene.shape status gives each shape's screen_box and px_per_unit: an assistant can tell if a stroke is too thin or off the frame.

control_note: These arguments add one shape to the current scene with scene.shape upsert. Ask scene.shape help for the full grammar, then check the result with scene.capture.
viewer_note: Requires the Polynite engine with SDF shapes (the scene.shape command). Shapes are saved inside the scene and replayed by its film; nothing is uploaded.

title: Widgets and six styles
description: The same panel - bracket, gauge, radar and bars - in hologram, neon, darkpunk, vaporwave, blueprint and amber, with their scanlines, glitch, gradient and CRT looks.
prompt:
Compare Polynite's six SDF shape styles with one widget panel.

- Over a small night studio, upsert six screen shapes 'panel-<style>' laid out in a 3 x 2 grid (at [0.2,0.3], [0.5,0.3], [0.8,0.3], [0.2,0.72], [0.5,0.72], [0.8,0.72], size 0.3).
- Each panel: a bracket (size [110,80]) labelled with its style, a gauge driven by '$v0', a small radar and six bars. Animate v0 from 0.1 to 0.9 with keys.
- Give each panel a style: hologram (raster and scan band), neon (glow and fringe), darkpunk (glitch, colour split, raster), vaporwave (pink to cyan gradient), blueprint (clean lines) and amber (CRT).
- Stagger their film steps by a quarter second so they trace in one after another, then record.
- Override any effect with fx: {scanlines, band, chroma, jitter, gradient:{axis, color}}.

experiments.title: Your own colours
experiments.text: Give a shape palette:[[r,g,b,a]...] to recolour its accents, or color:[r,g,b,a] on any item.

experiments.title: Mix the effects
experiments.text: fx:{gradient:{axis:'radial', color:[1,0.8,0.3,1]}, band:1} adds a radial gradient and a strong scan band to any style.

experiments.title: Glitch on cue
experiments.text: anim:{glitch:0.8, blink:2} makes the whole panel jump now and then and blink twice a second.

control_note: These arguments add one shape to the current scene with scene.shape upsert. Ask scene.shape help for the full grammar, then check the result with scene.capture.
viewer_note: Requires the Polynite engine with SDF shapes (the scene.shape command). Shapes are saved inside the scene and replayed by its film; nothing is uploaded.

title: A pavilion that follows the ground
description: Raise the land under a Japanese garden pavilion. Four independent feet adapt while its deck stays level, using one editable recipe and shared terrain operators.
prompt:
Create a Japanese garden pavilion that adapts to Polynite's infinite terrain.

- Check commands.recipe_terrain, then discover architecture.operators for spatial queries.
- Compose an assembly recipe with context:[{name:'ground',terrain:'infinite'}]. Sample four feet with height; keep the deck above their maximum plus floor_clearance.
- Choose dimensions in the recipe: an unbounded terrain has no footprint width or depth.
- Expose width, depth, roof curl and floor_clearance. Raise a broad patch of ground, then return it to the initial state in a five-second film.
- Keep the existing user scene and use stable IDs. Verify the contacts visually.
control_note: This edits the pavilion in the attached example. Discover its existing ID and parameter schema before editing a different scene. The operator samples terrain; the recipe chooses the deck and posts.

items.label: Ground height
items.hint: Raise the whole terrain. The pavilion follows without moving its camera.

experiments.title: Higher deck
experiments.text: Set floor_clearance to 0.6 under Scene settings > Living architecture > temple.

experiments.title: Another silhouette
experiments.text: Change width, depth, curl and overhang. The same support expressions still fit the feet.

experiments.title: A gentler slope
experiments.text: Change the raise cue depth from 4 to 2.2. Keep the ground edit broad enough for the terrain grid.

viewer_note: Requires commands.recipe_terrain. Press Play to compare flat and raised ground; use Adjust for the saved controls. Terrain queries use the finest near-field triangle grid, currently 4 m. Arbitrary imported meshes and continuous terrain deformation are outside this example.
